title: Your body language may shape who you are
speaker: Amy Cuddy

sentences.en: Translator: Joseph Geni Reviewer: Morton Bast So I want to start by offering you a free no-tech life hack,
sentences.zh: 首先我想要提供给你们一个免费的非科技的人生窍门你只需这样做改变你的姿势二分钟时间但在我要把它告诉你们之前，我想要请你们就你们的身体和你们身体的行为做一下自我审查那么你们之中有多少人正蜷缩着自己?

sentences.en: and all it requires of you is this: that you change your posture for two minutes.
sentences.zh: 那么你们之中有多少人正蜷缩着自己?或许你现在弓着背，还翘着二郎腿?或者双臂交叉有时候我们像这样抱住自己

sentences.en: But before I give it away, I want to ask you to right now do a little audit of your body and what you're doing with your body.
sentences.zh: 有时候我们像这样抱住自己有时候展开双臂(笑声)我看到你了(笑声)

sentences.en: So how many of you are sort of making yourselves smaller?
sentences.zh: 我看到你了(笑声)现在请大家专心在自己的身上

sentences.en: Maybe you're hunching, crossing your legs, maybe wrapping your ankles.
sentences.zh: 现在请大家专心在自己的身上我们等一下就会回溯刚刚的事希望你们可以稍微改变一下

sentences.en: Sometimes we hold onto our arms like this.
sentences.zh: 希望你们可以稍微改变一下这会让你的生活变得很不一样

sentences.en: Sometimes we spread out. (Laughter) I see you.
sentences.zh: 这会让你的生活变得很不一样所以，我们很真的很执着于肢体语言

sentences.en: So I want you to pay attention to what you're doing right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们很真的很执着于肢体语言特别是对别人的肢体语言感兴趣

sentences.en: We're going to come back to that in a few minutes, and I'm hoping that if you learn to tweak this a little bit, it could significantly change the way your life unfolds.
sentences.zh: 感兴趣你看，我们对(笑声)尴尬的互动，或一个微笑

sentences.en: So, we're really fascinated with body language, and we're particularly interested in other people's body language.
sentences.zh: 尴尬的互动，或一个微笑或轻蔑的一瞥，或奇怪的眨眼甚至是握手之类的事情感兴趣

sentences.en: You know, we're interested in, like, you know — (Laughter) — an awkward interaction, or a smile, or a contemptuous glance, or maybe a very awkward wink,
sentences.zh: 甚至是握手之类的事情感兴趣解说员:他们来到了唐宁街10号，看看这个这位幸运的警员可以和美国总统握手噢，还有来自....的总理?不(笑声) (掌声)

sentences.en: or maybe even something like a handshake.
sentences.zh: 来自....的总理?不(笑声) (掌声)(笑声) (掌声)Amy Cuddy:所以一个握手，或没有握手

sentences.zh: Amy Cuddy:所以一个握手，或没有握手

sentences.en: Here comes the Prime Minister -- No. (Laughter) (Applause) (Laughter) (Applause) Amy Cuddy: So a handshake, or the lack of a handshake, can have us talking for weeks and weeks and weeks.
sentences.zh: 即使BBC和纽约时报也不例外我们说到肢体行为或肢体语言时我们将之归纳为社会科学它就是一种语言，所以我们会想到沟通当我们想到沟通，我们就想到互动所以你现在的身体语言正在告诉我什么?

sentences.en: Even the BBC and The New York Times. So obviously when we think about nonverbal behavior, or body language -- but we call it nonverbals as social scientists -- it's language, so we think about communication.
sentences.zh: 所以你现在的身体语言正在告诉我什么?我的身体又是在向你传达什么?有很多理由让我们相信这些是有效的社会科学家花了很多时间求证肢体语言的效果

sentences.en: When we think about communication, we think about interactions.
sentences.zh: 求证肢体语言的效果或其它人的身体语言在判断方面的效应

sentences.en: So what is your body language communicating to me?
sentences.zh: 或其它人的身体语言在判断方面的效应而我们环视身体语言中的讯息做决定和推论

sentences.en: What's mine communicating to you? And there's a lot of reason to believe that this is a valid way to look at this.
sentences.zh: 而我们环视身体语言中的讯息做决定和推论这些结论可以预测生活中很有意义的结果像是我们雇用谁或给谁升职，邀请谁出去约会

sentences.en: So social scientists have spent a lot of time looking at the effects of our body language, or other people's body language, on judgments.
sentences.zh: 像是我们雇用谁或给谁升职，邀请谁出去约会举例而言，Tufts大学的研究员，Nalini Ambady表示

sentences.en: And we make sweeping judgments and inferences from body language.
sentences.zh: 举例而言，Tufts大学的研究员，Nalini Ambady表示人们观赏一部医生和患者互动的

sentences.en: And those judgments can predict really meaningful life outcomes like who we hire or promote, who we ask out on a date.
sentences.zh: 人们观赏一部医生和患者互动的30秒无声影片他们对该医生的和善观感可用来预测该复健师是否会被告上法庭

sentences.en: For example, Nalini Ambady, a researcher at Tufts University, shows that when people watch 30-second soundless clips of real physician-patient interactions,
sentences.zh: 可用来预测该复健师是否会被告上法庭跟这个医生能否胜任工作没有太大关系重点是我们喜不喜欢他和他们是如何与人互动的?进一步来说，普林斯顿的Alex Todorov 表示

sentences.en: their judgments of the physician's niceness predict whether or not that physician will be sued.
sentences.zh: 进一步来说，普林斯顿的Alex Todorov 表示我们对政治人物脸部的喜好判断大概可用来对美国参议院和美国州长的

sentences.en: So it doesn't have to do so much with whether or not that physician was incompetent, but do we like that person and how they interacted?
sentences.zh: 大概可用来对美国参议院和美国州长的竞选结果做70%的预测甚至就网络上

sentences.en: Even more dramatic, Alex Todorov at Princeton has shown us that judgments of political candidates' faces in just one second predict 70 percent of U.S. Senate and gubernatorial race outcomes,
sentences.zh: 甚至就网络上在线聊天时使用的表情符号可以帮助你从交谈中得到更多信息所以你千万别弄巧成拙，对吧?当我们提起肢体语言，我们就想到我们如何论断别人

sentences.en: and even, let's go digital, emoticons used well in online negotiations can lead you to claim more value from that negotiation.
sentences.zh: 当我们提起肢体语言，我们就想到我们如何论断别人别人如何论断我们以及后果会是什么我们往往忘记这点，受到肢体动作所影响的那群观众就是我们自己我们也往往受自己的肢体动作，想法

sentences.en: If you use them poorly, bad idea. Right?
sentences.zh: 我们也往往受自己的肢体动作，想法感觉和心理所影响

sentences.en: So when we think of nonverbals, we think of how we judge others, how they judge us and what the outcomes are.
sentences.zh: 感觉和心理所影响所以究竟我说的是怎样的非语言?我是一位社会心理学家，我研究偏见

sentences.en: We tend to forget, though, the other audience that's influenced by our nonverbals, and that's ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我是一位社会心理学家，我研究偏见我在一所极具竞争力的商业学院上课因此无可避免地对权力动力学感到着迷

sentences.en: We are also influenced by our nonverbals, our thoughts and our feelings and our physiology.
sentences.zh: 因此无可避免地对权力动力学感到着迷特别是在非语言表达

sentences.en: So what nonverbals am I talking about? I'm a social psychologist. I study prejudice, and I teach at a competitive business school, so it was inevitable that I would become interested in power dynamics.
sentences.zh: 特别是在非语言表达对权力和支配的领域权力和支配的非语言表达究竟是什么?嗯，让我细细道来在动物王国里，它们和扩张有关所以你尽可能的让自己变大，你向外伸展

sentences.en: I became especially interested in nonverbal expressions of power and dominance.
sentences.zh: 所以你尽可能的让自己变大，你向外伸展占满空间，基本上就是展开关于展开，我说真的

sentences.en: And what are nonverbal expressions of power and dominance?
sentences.zh: 关于展开，我说真的透视动物世界，这不仅局限于灵长类

sentences.en: Well, this is what they are. So in the animal kingdom, they are about expanding.
sentences.zh: 透视动物世界，这不仅局限于灵长类人类也干同样的事(笑声)

sentences.en: So you make yourself big, you stretch out, you take up space, you're basically opening up.
sentences.zh: 人类也干同样的事(笑声)不论是他们长期掌权或是在某个时间点感到权力高涨他们都这么做

sentences.en: It's about opening up. And this is true across the animal kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他们都这么做特别有趣的原因是它让我们明白权力的展现从来是如此地一致，不管古今世界

sentences.en: It's not just limited to primates. And humans do the same thing. (Laughter) So they do this both when they have power sort of chronically, and also when they're feeling powerful in the moment.
sentences.zh: 它让我们明白权力的展现从来是如此地一致，不管古今世界这种展现，被认为是一种荣耀Jessica Tracy研究表示视力良好无碍和先天视障的人

sentences.en: And this one is especially interesting because it really shows us how universal and old these expressions of power are.
sentences.zh: 和先天视障的人在赢得比赛时都做了同样的事当他们跨过终点线赢得比赛之际无论能否看的见

sentences.en: This expression, which is known as pride, Jessica Tracy has studied.
sentences.zh: 无论能否看的见他们都做这样的动作双臂呈V字型朝上，下巴微微抬起

sentences.en: She shows that people who are born with sight and people who are congenitally blind do this when they win at a physical competition.
sentences.zh: 双臂呈V字型朝上，下巴微微抬起那我们感到无助的时候呢?我们的行为正相反我们封闭起来。我们把自己蜷起来让自己变得小一点，最好别碰到别人

sentences.en: So when they cross the finish line and they've won, it doesn't matter if they've never seen anyone do it.
sentences.zh: 让自己变得小一点，最好别碰到别人这再一次证明，人类和动物都做同样的事

sentences.en: They do this. So the arms up in the V, the chin is slightly lifted.
sentences.zh: 这再一次证明，人类和动物都做同样的事这就是当你有力量和没力量时的行为

sentences.en: What do we do when we feel powerless? We do exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 这就是当你有力量和没力量时的行为所以当力量来临时我们会迎合别人的非语言

sentences.en: We close up. We wrap ourselves up. We make ourselves small.
sentences.zh: 我们会迎合别人的非语言若有人之于我们相对权重时

sentences.en: We don't want to bump into the person next to us.
sentences.zh: 若有人之于我们相对权重时我们倾向把自己变得较小，不会模仿他们

sentences.en: So again, both animals and humans do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向把自己变得较小，不会模仿他们我们做和他们正相反的事情

sentences.en: And this is what happens when you put together high and low power.
sentences.zh: 我们做和他们正相反的事情当我在课堂上观察这么现象时

sentences.en: So what we tend to do when it comes to power is that we complement the other's nonverbals.
sentences.zh: 当我在课堂上观察这么现象时你猜我发现什么?我发现MBA的学生

sentences.en: So if someone is being really powerful with us, we tend to make ourselves smaller. We don't mirror them.
sentences.zh: 你猜我发现什么?我发现MBA的学生真的很会就充分利用肢体语言你会看到有些人像是统治者

sentences.en: We do the opposite of them. So I'm watching this behavior in the classroom, and what do I notice?
sentences.zh: 你会看到有些人像是统治者走进房间，课程开始之前一屁股坐在正中间好像他们真的很想占据整个教室似的

sentences.en: I notice that MBA students really exhibit the full range of power nonverbals.
sentences.zh: 好像他们真的很想占据整个教室似的当他们坐下的时候，身体会展开像这样举手有些人则不然

sentences.en: So you have people who are like caricatures of alphas, really coming into the room, they get right into the middle of the room before class even starts, like they really want to occupy space.
sentences.zh: 有些人则不然他们一走进来你就会发现从他们的脸和身体你会发现他们坐在椅子上的时候把自己变得很萎靡然后举手的时候是这种姿势

sentences.en: When they sit down, they're sort of spread out.
sentences.zh: 然后举手的时候是这种姿势我观察到很多事情

sentences.en: They raise their hands like this. You have other people who are virtually collapsing when they come in. As soon they come in, you see it.
sentences.zh: 我观察到很多事情其中一件，不令人惊讶就是跟性别差异有关女人比男人更容易出现这种状况

sentences.en: You see it on their faces and their bodies, and they sit in their chair and they make themselves tiny, and they go like this when they raise their hand.
sentences.zh: 女人比男人更容易出现这种状况女人一般比较容易比男人感到无力这并不太令人意外。然而我发现的另一件事是

sentences.en: I notice a couple of things about this. One, you're not going to be surprised.
sentences.zh: 这并不太令人意外。然而我发现的另一件事是这似乎也跟

sentences.en: It seems to be related to gender. So women are much more likely to do this kind of thing than men.
sentences.zh: 这似乎也跟学生参与的程度高低有关就MBA的课来说这真的非常重要

sentences.en: Women feel chronically less powerful than men, so this is not surprising.
sentences.zh: 就MBA的课来说这真的非常重要因为课堂参与程度要占成绩的一半所以商学院一直以来都为此伤脑筋

sentences.en: But the other thing I noticed is that it also seemed to be related to the extent to which the students were participating, and how well they were participating.
sentences.zh: 所以商学院一直以来都为此伤脑筋入学的时候男生女生是不分轩轾的可是成绩出来却有这些性别差异而看起来却有一部分原因和参与度有关

sentences.en: And this is really important in the MBA classroom, because participation counts for half the grade.
sentences.zh: 而看起来却有一部分原因和参与度有关所以我开始思索，好吧

sentences.en: So business schools have been struggling with this gender grade gap.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始思索，好吧这群人一开始进来是这样，他们参与其中那有没有可能让大家来假装

sentences.en: You get these equally qualified women and men coming in and then you get these differences in grades, and it seems to be partly attributable to participation.
sentences.zh: 那有没有可能让大家来假装让他们更加参与进来?我在Berkeley的主要合作研究伙伴，Dana Carney

sentences.en: So I started to wonder, you know, okay, so you have these people coming in like this, and they're participating.
sentences.zh: 我在Berkeley的主要合作研究伙伴，Dana Carney我很想知道，你能假装直到你成功吗？譬如说，只做一下下然后就体验到一个

sentences.en: Is it possible that we could get people to fake it and would it lead them to participate more?
sentences.zh: 譬如说，只做一下下然后就体验到一个让你感到更加充满力量的结果所以得知非语言如何掌控他人

sentences.en: So my main collaborator Dana Carney, who's at Berkeley, and I really wanted to know, can you fake it till you make it?
sentences.zh: 所以得知非语言如何掌控他人对我们的想法和感受。有很多证据可以证明但我们的问题是，我们非语言的部分是否真的掌控我们对自己的想法和感受?

sentences.en: Like, can you do this just for a little while and actually experience a behavioral outcome that makes you seem more powerful?
sentences.zh: 是否真的掌控我们对自己的想法和感受?这里确实有些证据可以表明举例来说，当我们高兴的时候我们会笑

sentences.en: So we know that our nonverbals govern how other people think and feel about us. There's a lot of evidence.
sentences.zh: 举例来说，当我们高兴的时候我们会笑但同样地，当我们含着一只笔练习笑容的时候我们也会感到开心

sentences.en: But our question really was, do our nonverbals govern how we think and feel about ourselves?
sentences.zh: 我们也会感到开心这说明这是相互的。说到力量的时候

sentences.en: There's some evidence that they do. So, for example, we smile when we feel happy, but also, when we're forced to smile by holding a pen in our teeth like this, it makes us feel happy.
sentences.zh: 这说明这是相互的。说到力量的时候亦是如此。所以当我们感到充满力量的时候你更加可能会这样做，但你也可能假装自己很有力量

sentences.en: So it goes both ways. When it comes to power, it also goes both ways.
sentences.zh: 假装自己很有力量然后真的感到力量强大那第二个问题就是，你看

sentences.en: So when you feel powerful, you're more likely to do this, but it's also possible that when you pretend to be powerful, you are more likely to actually feel powerful.
sentences.zh: 那第二个问题就是，你看我们知道心理状态会影响我们的身体那身体是否能影响心理呢?这里所说的心理充满力量究竟指的是什么?我指的是想法和感觉

sentences.en: So the second question really was, you know, so we know that our minds change our bodies, but is it also true that our bodies change our minds?
sentences.zh: 我指的是想法和感觉和可以组成我们想法和感受的实际事物我这里是指荷尔蒙。我指的是这个充满力量和没有力量的心智

sentences.en: And when I say minds, in the case of the powerful, what am I talking about?
sentences.zh: 充满力量和没有力量的心智是什么样的呢?毫不令人意外，心理坚强的人往往

sentences.en: So I'm talking about thoughts and feelings and the sort of physiological things that make up our thoughts and feelings, and in my case, that's hormones. I look at hormones.
sentences.zh: 毫不令人意外，心理坚强的人往往比较果断，自信，且乐观就连在赌注里也觉得他们会赢

sentences.en: So what do the minds of the powerful versus the powerless look like?
sentences.zh: 就连在赌注里也觉得他们会赢他们也倾向于能够抽象地思考

sentences.en: So powerful people tend to be, not surprisingly, more assertive and more confident, more optimistic.
sentences.zh: 他们也倾向于能够抽象地思考所以这其中有很大区别。他们更敢于冒险充满力量与否的心智二者存有许多不同生理上两个关键的贺尔蒙

sentences.en: They actually feel they're going to win even at games of chance.
sentences.zh: 生理上两个关键的贺尔蒙睾丸酮，是一种支配荷尔蒙

sentences.en: They also tend to be able to think more abstractly.
sentences.zh: 睾丸酮，是一种支配荷尔蒙可的松，是一种压力荷尔蒙

sentences.en: So there are a lot of differences. They take more risks.
sentences.zh: 可的松，是一种压力荷尔蒙我们发现

sentences.en: There are a lot of differences between powerful and powerless people.
sentences.zh: 我们发现灵长类的雄性首领

sentences.en: Physiologically, there also are differences on two key hormones: testosterone, which is the dominance hormone, and cortisol, which is the stress hormone.
sentences.zh: 灵长类的雄性首领有高浓度的睪丸酮和低浓度的可的松相同情形也在强而有力的领导人身上可见

sentences.en: So what we find is that high-power alpha males in primate hierarchies have high testosterone and low cortisol, and powerful and effective leaders
sentences.zh: 强而有力的领导人身上可见这表示什么? 当你想到力量人们往往只想到睪丸酮因为它代表支配统治但力量其实是在于你如何应对压力所以你会想要一个

sentences.en: also have high testosterone and low cortisol.
sentences.zh: 所以你会想要一个有着很高浓度的睪丸酮但同时又高度紧张的领导吗?

sentences.en: So what does that mean? When you think about power, people tended to think only about testosterone, because that was about dominance.
sentences.zh: 有着很高浓度的睪丸酮但同时又高度紧张的领导吗?大概不会是吧?你会希望那个人是充满力量，肯定果断且知道如何支配但不是非常紧张，或是懒洋洋的

sentences.en: But really, power is also about how you react to stress.
sentences.zh: 但不是非常紧张，或是懒洋洋的灵长类动物的金字塔里

sentences.en: So do you want the high-power leader that's dominant, high on testosterone, but really stress reactive?
sentences.zh: 灵长类动物的金字塔里如果一个首领想要掌控这个种群

sentences.en: Probably not, right? You want the person who's powerful and assertive and dominant, but not very stress reactive, the person who's laid back.
sentences.zh: 如果一个首领想要掌控这个种群或取代原先的首领几天之内，那一方体内的睪丸酮会大大地上升

sentences.en: So we know that in primate hierarchies, if an alpha needs to take over, if an individual needs to take over an alpha role sort of suddenly,
sentences.zh: 几天之内，那一方体内的睪丸酮会大大地上升而其可的松会剧烈地下降身体影响心理之例，由此可见一斑至少就表面而言是如此同时角色的转换也会影响心智

sentences.en: within a few days, that individual's testosterone has gone up significantly and his cortisol has dropped significantly.

sentences.en: So we have this evidence, both that the body can shape the mind, at least at the facial level, and also that role changes can shape the mind.
